newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikko Sec to provide 147.5 bln yen in aid to units.
newsitem.headline: Nikko Sec to provide 147.5 bln yen in aid to units.

text.p: Nikko Securities Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would provide 147.5 billion yen in financial aid to its three non-bank affiliates.
The third-biggest Japanese broker also said in a statement that it would post a special loss of 147.5 billion yen in the current business year, ending next March 31.

Nikko Securities said in a statement that the company decided to help the non-bank affiliates dispose of their problem loans as soon as possible in a bid to maintain the credibility of Nikko Securities and the affiliates.
It also said that by disposing of the problem loans at the affiliates, Nikko Securities will be able to strengthen its business development in future.
The three affiliates are Kyodo Teito Shoken Co Ltd, Nikko Credit Co Ltd and Nikko Fudosan Co Ltd.
Nikko will provide 82.1 billion yen in financial aid to Kyodo Teito Shoken, 47.7 billion yen to Nikko Credit and 17.7 billion yen to Nikko Fudosan, it said.
Nikko said it would sell securities holdings to raise funds for the aid.
Nikko now estimates it will post 95 billion yen in parent net losses in 1996/97 to deal with the financial aid, against its previous estimate of parent net profits of 24 billion yen.
